source.title: Memory3: Language Modeling with Explicit Memory
source.authors: Hongkang Yang; Zehao Lin; Wenjin Wang; Hao Wu; Zhi-Yu Li; Bo Tang; Wen-Qiang Wei; Jinbo Wang; Zeyun Tang; Shichao Song; Chen-Yang Xi; Yu Yu; Kai Chen; Fei-Yu Xiong; Linpeng Tang; E. Weinan

record.tranche_reason: The study compares training losses across model shapes at similar parameter counts, which bears on V4, but it does not reproduce the scaling-law measurements.
record.gate_note: The study cites scaling-law work but does not test power-law scaling, extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocation. Its warmup/continual-train loss comparisons and reports of loss divergence are training-loss results, not held-out scaling-law tests; they are not separate rows.
record.test_reason: The paper is about explicit-memory LLMs and cites scaling laws only in passing. Its one bearing result is a controlled shape ablation (Fig. 10): training-loss curves of 2.1–2.4B models with different depth/head ratios. This bears weakly on V4 in a new setting (Chinese/English data, GQA, warmup stage of a two-stage scheme). The ablation was run to choose the model's own shape and is reported only as a figure.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors report that loss decreased slightly faster with L:H ≈ 1 than with other ratios, and adopted that ratio. They say the comparison is not definite because it covers only the warmup stage, and the ranking may change once explicit memory is introduced.
record.recipe_differences: A limited shape comparison using training-loss curves, rather than held-out scaling-law fits or compute-optimal allocation measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that the ranking across shapes may change between warmup and continual training.

fits_no_version.finding: Pretraining became more unstable, with more loss spikes, when head dimension dh ≤ 64. The authors note data quality may also matter.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some shape choices (small head dimension) affect training stability even if they change converged loss little.

record.problems: The shape comparison is limited to the warmup stage and parameter sizes 2.1 ∼ 2.4B; the authors say it is not definitive and provide no uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: Shape effects after the continual-train stage, where the authors say the ranking may change. Held-out loss. Shapes beyond the few L:H ratios near 2.1–2.4B. Width/MLP ratios beyond W = d.
Entire version; benchmark comparisons across models are not a scaling analysis.

record.verdict_notes: The record's limits_scope label is removed. The authors' caution that the ranking could change in continual training is an untested condition, not a result showing V4 fails. The relation could arguably be downgraded, because the experiment is a design-selection ablation with no numbers. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of larger-run loss from power-law fits on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation as a function of compute.
The comparison covers a limited set of shapes and parameter sizes during warmup, not a wide range of architectures or held-out loss.
Other modalities and training regimes as tests of the same power-law form.
Predictability of downstream performance from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup and fitting choices, and departures from power-law curves.

rows.subject: models with different shapes (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared training-loss curves across model shapes at similar parameter sizes.

conditions.value: different shapes; the text reports L:H ≈ 1 versus other ratios

rows.value: L:H ≈ 1 showed a slightly faster decrease in loss
rows.note: Aggregate comparison; the text describes the trend but does not give per-shape numerical results. The authors caution that this is only the warmup stage and the ranking may change during continual training.
rows.check: State should be observed, not partial. V4 predicts small loss differences across shapes at fixed size, and the text says loss fell only 'slightly more rapidly' with L:H ≈ 1. Caveats: the measure is training loss, not held-out loss. Results are figure-only with no numbers or uncertainty. The exact shapes and ratios compared are not listed in the text (only l44h40d80 is named). The comparison doubles as the hyperparameter selection for the paper's own model.

relationships.condition: Warmup-stage training loss of 2.1–2.4B models with varying L:H ratios (dh=80, GQA)
relationships.reason: Authors describe the loss differences across shapes as slight, with L:H ≈ 1 marginally faster (r1). The evidence is figure-only and unquantified.
relationships.display_finding: Loss differences across shapes were slight, with a layer-to-head ratio near 1 learning marginally faster.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: tested model shapes during warmup at 2.1 ∼ 2.4B parameters
reader_labels.reason: The authors describe the loss differences across tested shapes as slight; this is a limited-range result (r1).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The authors state that the comparison is not definite and that the ranking may change during continual training, so it does not establish insensitivity across a wide range (r1).
